newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Brig Gen Raymundo Jarque surfaces to join the communist National Democratic Front panel in peace negotiations with the government (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos leaves for a 10-day, five-nation tour of South Asia and the Middle East in search of new markets, investments and technology cooperation. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Visiting South African president Nelson Mandela foresees stronger Philippine-South African relations after his visit to the country. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Vice president Joseph Estrada is considering to file contempt charges against Pangasinan congressman Simeon Valdez for pushing for a Charter change despite a Supreme Court order stopping the move (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Inflation in February is projected to soften to 4.94 percent from 5.0 percent in January and 11.8 percent in February last year, analysts polled by Reuters say.
- Benpres Holdings Corp is planning to spin off its media interests to allow foreign investors to invest in Benpres, chief finance officer J. Xavier Gonzales says (TODAY)
- The Department of Trade and Industry has proposed a bill to increase fiscal incentives to export-oriented firms despite a move by the Department of Finance to cut down tax perks. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Philippine Central Bank is planning to put limit the exposure of local banks to the real estate sector equivalent to 30 percent of their loanable portfolio (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
